conditional_questions.question: How are Total cholesterol and HDL (good cholesterol) connected?

short_description: Total cholesterol is the full amount of cholesterol travelling in your blood, counting both the helpful and the less helpful kinds together.
what_happens_inside_my_body: Cholesterol is a waxy fat your body needs to build cells and make some hormones and vitamin D.
Your liver makes most of it, and the rest comes from food.
Cholesterol cannot dissolve in blood, so it travels inside tiny carrier particles. LDL and HDL are the best known.
why_this_test_matters: Too much cholesterol in the wrong carriers can slowly build up in artery walls and narrow them.
Total cholesterol is usually checked as part of a lipid profile to judge heart and blood vessel health.

low: A lower total is often a good sign for the heart. Very low values are uncommon and can occasionally go with an overactive thyroid, poor nutrition or some liver conditions.
normal: Your total cholesterol is inside the lab's range. Heart risk still depends on how it is split between LDL and HDL, and on things like blood pressure, smoking and diabetes.
high: A higher total usually means more cholesterol is circulating. It may come from LDL, which can build up in arteries, or partly from HDL, which is helpful. Your LDL and HDL results show which one is driving it.
reference_unavailable: Your report did not include a reference range for total cholesterol, so CURA cannot say whether it is high or low.

clinical_limitations: Total cholesterol adds HDL and LDL together, so on its own it cannot show whether the cholesterol is mostly the helpful or the harmful kind.

diet_and_lifestyle: Foods rich in saturated fat, such as fatty meat, butter, ghee and many fried or packaged snacks, tend to raise blood cholesterol.
Soluble fibre from oats, dal, beans and fruit helps your body clear cholesterol.
everyday_support: Choose oils like mustard, groundnut or olive oil more often than ghee, butter or vanaspati. Unsaturated fats are kinder to blood cholesterol.
Add a bowl of dal, beans, oats or vegetables to most meals. Their fibre helps carry cholesterol out of your body.
Try to move for about 30 minutes on most days, such as a brisk walk. Regular activity helps raise HDL and lower other blood fats.
when_to_seek_medical_advice: Talk to a doctor if your cholesterol is high and you also have diabetes or high blood pressure.
Also talk to a doctor if a parent or sibling had a heart attack or stroke at a young age.

factor_explanations.how_it_acts: Genes set how much cholesterol your liver makes and how fast it clears LDL, so some people run high even with careful eating.
Ghee, butter, cream, fatty meat and many fried snacks lead the liver to clear less LDL from the blood, which raises the total.
Extra body fat, especially around the waist, tends to raise LDL and triglycerides and lower HDL.
Regular activity mainly lifts HDL and lowers triglycerides, which changes the mix inside the total.
An underactive thyroid slows LDL clearance, so cholesterol can rise until the thyroid is treated.
Statins and similar medicines lower LDL, which brings the total down.

keeping_healthy: Keep doing what supports your blood vessels: regular movement, not smoking, and meals built around vegetables, dal, whole grains and nuts.
Cholesterol can change over years with weight, age and menopause, so repeat checks at the interval your doctor suggests matter even when this result is good.
lowering_risk: Blood pressure, blood sugar and smoking add to the same artery risk as cholesterol, so working on any of them protects your heart.
If close family members had heart disease young, tell your doctor. It changes how your results are judged.
common_misconceptions: A normal total does not always mean a healthy pattern. A high HDL can hide a raised LDL inside a normal-looking total, so the separate results matter more.
Thin people can have high cholesterol too, because genes play a large part.
reference_range_note: Many labs print a desirable cut-off rather than a range drawn from healthy people. The level a doctor aims for depends on your overall heart risk, including blood pressure, blood sugar, smoking and family history, so the same number can be fine for one person and too high for another.

conditional_questions.question: How are HDL (good cholesterol) and LDL (calculated bad cholesterol) connected?

short_description: HDL is often called good cholesterol. This test measures how much cholesterol is carried by HDL particles, which help remove extra cholesterol from your body.
what_happens_inside_my_body: HDL particles pick up spare cholesterol from tissues and artery walls.
HDL carries it back to your liver, which clears it from your body.
This test measures how much cholesterol is inside HDL particles. It does not measure how well those particles are doing their clean-up work.
why_this_test_matters: Low HDL is linked with a higher chance of heart disease.
Doctors look at HDL together with LDL and triglycerides to judge heart risk.

low: Low HDL means less cholesterol is being cleared away. It often goes with low activity, smoking, extra weight around the waist, high triglycerides or insulin resistance.
normal: Your HDL is inside the healthy range, which is encouraging. It is still read together with your LDL, triglycerides and other heart risk factors, because a good HDL does not cancel out a high LDL.
high: Higher HDL is generally linked with lower heart risk. Very high levels, above about 100 mg/dL, do not add extra protection and in some people come from inherited patterns or heavy alcohol use.
reference_unavailable: Your report did not include a reference range for HDL (good cholesterol), so CURA cannot say whether it is high or low.

clinical_limitations: HDL measures the cholesterol inside HDL particles, not how well those particles work. A good HDL result does not cancel out a high LDL.

diet_and_lifestyle: Regular physical activity and stopping smoking are among the most reliable ways HDL rises.
Diets high in refined carbohydrates and sugar tend to go with lower HDL and higher triglycerides.
everyday_support: Build movement into your day, such as walking after meals or taking stairs. Regular activity is one of the few habits known to lift HDL.
If you smoke, ask about support to stop. Stopping smoking helps HDL recover and protects your blood vessels.
Cut back on sugary drinks, sweets and refined flour. They push triglycerides up, which usually pulls HDL down.
when_to_seek_medical_advice: Talk to a doctor if HDL is low alongside high LDL, high triglycerides, high blood sugar or high blood pressure, as these together raise heart risk.

factor_explanations.how_it_acts: Regular aerobic activity such as brisk walking is one of the few habits shown to raise HDL.
Smoking lowers HDL; stopping lets it recover.
Extra fat around the waist goes with lower HDL; losing some of it can raise HDL a little.
When triglycerides are high, HDL particles are reshaped and cleared faster, so HDL usually falls.
Genes strongly shape HDL, which is why some people have low or very high HDL despite their habits.
Some medicines, such as anabolic steroids and some blood pressure tablets, can lower HDL.

keeping_healthy: Regular activity and not smoking are the habits most linked with keeping HDL healthy.
If you do not drink alcohol, there is no reason to start to raise HDL.
lowering_risk: Blood pressure, blood sugar and smoking add to the same artery risk as cholesterol, so working on any of them protects your heart.
If close family members had heart disease young, tell your doctor. It changes how your results are judged.
common_misconceptions: More HDL is not always better. Raising HDL with medicines has not lowered heart attacks, so doctors do not treat HDL as a target on its own.
HDL concentration is not the same as HDL working well. Two people with the same HDL number can have particles that clear cholesterol differently.
reference_range_note: Healthy HDL is usually above 40 mg/dL for men and above 50 mg/dL for women. Some reports print one cut-off for everyone, so check which applies to you.

conditional_questions.question: How are Triglycerides and VLDL cholesterol connected?

short_description: Triglycerides are the most common type of fat in your blood. Your body stores spare energy from food as triglycerides and uses them as fuel between meals.
what_happens_inside_my_body: When you eat more energy than you need right away, your body turns the extra into triglycerides.
Triglycerides are stored in fat cells and released later when you need energy.
Sugar, refined carbohydrates and alcohol are easily turned into triglycerides by the liver.
why_this_test_matters: High triglycerides are linked with heart disease, fatty liver and insulin resistance.
Very high levels can inflame the pancreas, an organ behind the stomach that helps digestion.

low: Low triglycerides are usually not a concern. They can go with a low-fat diet, regular exercise, and occasionally an overactive thyroid or poor absorption of food.
normal: Your triglycerides are inside the lab's range, which suggests your body is handling fats from food well at the moment.
high: Higher triglycerides often reflect a recent meal, extra sugar or refined carbohydrates, alcohol, extra weight or insulin resistance. If you did not fast before the test, the result can read higher.
reference_unavailable: Your report did not include a reference range for triglycerides, so CURA cannot say whether it is high or low.

clinical_limitations: Triglycerides change a lot after eating and drinking alcohol, so one result may not reflect your usual level.

Alcohol raises triglycerides strongly in some people, even in modest amounts.
Regular activity helps your muscles burn triglycerides for fuel.

Fill half your plate with vegetables and choose smaller portions of rice, roti or bread. This lowers the sugar load your liver has to process.

When you eat more sugar or refined flour than you burn, your liver turns the extra into triglycerides.
Alcohol is turned into fat by the liver and can push triglycerides up sharply, even in moderate amounts for some people.
Extra weight, especially around the waist, goes with higher triglycerides.
When insulin works poorly, the liver makes more triglyceride-rich particles and the body clears them more slowly.
An underactive thyroid can slow how quickly triglycerides are cleared.

keeping_healthy: Keep doing what supports your blood vessels: regular movement, not smoking, and meals built around vegetables, dal, whole grains and nuts.

lowering_risk: Triglycerides respond quickly to cutting sugary drinks, sweets, refined flour and alcohol, often within weeks.

common_misconceptions: Triglycerides are not only about fatty food. Sugar, refined carbohydrates and alcohol often raise them more.
reference_range_note: Many labs print a desirable cut-off rather than a range drawn from healthy people. diet_and_lifestyle: Diet, activity, sleep and body weight all affect how well insulin works and so your fasting sugar.
everyday_support: Fill half your plate with vegetables and pair rice or roti with dal, curd, paneer, eggs or other protein. This slows how quickly sugar enters your blood.
Swap sugary drinks, sweets and refined flour for water, whole fruit and whole grains like millets or brown rice. These cause smaller sugar spikes.
Take a 10 to 15 minute walk after main meals. Physical activity helps your body manage blood sugar, and sugar after a walk is often lower than before.
Aim for enough sleep. A healthy weight, regular activity and enough sleep are part of the lifestyle that may help prevent insulin resistance.
when_to_seek_medical_advice: Talk to a doctor if your blood sugar results are above range, so they can check for prediabetes or diabetes. Both are common and often have no symptoms.
Seek care promptly if you have extreme thirst, passing a lot of urine, unexplained weight loss, blurred vision, or feel shaky, sweaty or confused from low sugar.

When cells respond poorly to insulin, the liver releases more glucose overnight and fasting sugar creeps up.
Extra weight, especially around the waist, makes insulin work less well.
